project.name: SweK Engine
project.summary: A browser game and simulation engine with hundreds of pages (3D worlds, physics, ship duels, avatars, home dashboards), a local Node server (the ai-bridge) that connects the pages to AI models, the home, phones and installers, and a large set of self-checks and research studies that hold every claim to a measurement.

nodes.label: The pages
nodes.summary: Every page you open in the browser: the main engine, the hubs, and hundreds of single-purpose demos, games and dashboards.

nodes.label: Main engine page
nodes.summary: The big engine page and its startup script, which wires the world, physics, brains and panels together.

nodes.label: Hubs and control panels
nodes.summary: The pages that lead to everything else: the server control page, the home page, the panels board and the install panel host.

nodes.label: Demo scripts
nodes.summary: Scripted showcases and diagnostics that run the engine end to end.

nodes.label: Ship games (EV and BZ)
nodes.summary: Two self-contained games inside the engine: an Escape-Velocity-style space trader and a tank battle.

nodes.label: Engine core
nodes.summary: The shared machinery every page draws on: drawing to the screen, effects, the world and terrain, sound, text, input and the entity system.

nodes.label: Rendering
nodes.summary: Draws every frame on the graphics card (WebGPU and WebGL): denoising, upscaling, frame generation, lighting and shaders.

nodes.label: Visual effects
nodes.summary: Effects layered on a scene: avatar looks, FSR upscaling, voxelizing, nebulae, fractures, wormholes.

nodes.label: Worlds and terrain
nodes.summary: Builds the places the engine shows: voxel chunks, terrain, oceans, maps, dungeons and the meshes they are made of.

nodes.label: Engine foundations
nodes.summary: The building blocks underneath: the entity system, commands, maths, input, animation, navigation, sound and text.

nodes.label: Networking and multiplayer
nodes.summary: How a page finds the local server and shares a game or a picture with other machines.

nodes.label: Physics and simulation
nodes.summary: The physical models the pages run: rigid bodies, cloth and soft bodies, fluids, particles, heat, electromagnetism, black holes and whole-world simulations.

nodes.label: Bodies, cloth and mechanics
nodes.summary: Solid things moving and colliding: position-based dynamics, mechanics, box physics, characters and meshes.

nodes.label: Fluids and particles
nodes.summary: Water, smoke, sand and molecules: particle fluids, material-point and molecular-dynamics methods, lattice fluids.

nodes.label: Fields, heat and space
nodes.summary: Things that spread through space: electromagnetism, heat, black holes, and scans through a body (tomography).

nodes.label: World simulations
nodes.summary: Whole scenarios that run over time: populations, civilisations, monsters, cells, the game of life.

nodes.label: Brains and AI
nodes.summary: What makes things decide: connectome-wired brains (the fly-wired gunners and helms), learning agents, the ship duel that tests them, and the AI agents that command the world.

nodes.label: Ship duels and gunners
nodes.summary: The battleship duel, the gunner and helm networks the duel page carries, and the trained pilot.

nodes.label: Learning
nodes.summary: Reinforcement learning and the training loops brains are improved with.

nodes.label: World agents
nodes.summary: Agents that act inside the world: they queue up commands, pass them on, and drive faces and expressions.

nodes.label: Shared page widgets
nodes.summary: Panels and widgets many pages share: gauges, the docked status bar, settings, the install panel, avatars and chat.

nodes.label: Install panel
nodes.summary: Lists every tool, model and app SweK can install and runs the install through the local server.

nodes.label: Gauges and dock
nodes.summary: The docked gauges, the stats bar and the dials that show the machine's state.

nodes.label: Local server (ai-bridge)
nodes.summary: The Node server that runs on your own machine: it connects the pages to AI models, your home, your phone and TV, and runs installs on request.

nodes.label: The server itself
nodes.summary: The one big server file that receives every request from the pages and hands it to the right helper.

nodes.label: Installers
nodes.summary: Runs the install catalog: installs from GitHub releases, apps, Python and model downloads, with checks on which machines each one can run on.

nodes.label: Home, phone and TV
nodes.summary: Talks to Home Assistant, Android phones, TVs and devices found on the network.

nodes.label: AI model helpers
nodes.summary: Connects to local and cloud AI models: Ollama, Gemini, Whisper, MLX, Voxtral and others.

nodes.label: Scrapers
nodes.summary: Fetches pages and data from the web for the engine's feeds.

nodes.label: Ship and research tools
nodes.summary: Command-line tools for releasing versions and for the registered studies that decide what the pages carry.

nodes.label: Registered studies
nodes.summary: Each study is written down before it is flown, read once, and decides one thing on the page (the take* and train* tools).

nodes.label: Release and checking tools
nodes.summary: Version bumps, the changelog, claim checks, the gate sweeps and the real-GPU runs.

nodes.label: Roundhouse
nodes.summary: Peer rounds: experiments run across machines and their reports.

nodes.label: Render QA
nodes.summary: Opens pages in a headless browser, screenshots them and checks the picture.

nodes.label: Self-checks
nodes.summary: Every *-selfcheck file: a gate that holds one file's claims and must pass before a version ships. About a third of all the code.

nodes.label: Companion apps
nodes.summary: Smaller apps beside the engine: Home Assistant add-on, Tasker phone bridge, the K-pop listener, a Raycast extension, the cloud meeting server and helper libraries.

nodes.label: Cloud meeting server
nodes.summary: A small server in the cloud that lets SweK machines find each other and open video connections.

nodes.label: Home and phone apps
nodes.summary: The Home Assistant add-on and the Tasker bridge for an Android phone.

nodes.label: three.js

nodes.label: Headless browser (Playwright)
nodes.summary: Runs pages in Chromium for the gates and render QA.

nodes.label: Python science stack

nodes.label: Google Gemini

nodes.summary: Where installs and releases are fetched from.

nodes.label: MQTT
nodes.summary: The way home devices send each other messages.

nodes.label: Home Assistant
nodes.summary: Your home's automation hub, reached by the server.

flows.title: Installing a tool from the panel

steps.note: You tick a row in the install panel and press Install.
The page sends the row's id to the local server.
The server re-reads the catalog, checks the row can run on this machine, and runs its commands.
Most rows clone a repository or download a release from GitHub.

flows.title: How a study changes the duel page

steps.note: A study is written down with its pairs, its arms and what it will decide, before anything is flown.
Its gate holds that registration, and broken copies of the study are tried against the gate until every one is caught.
The study flies the duels through the brains, thousands of pairs at a time.
The reading is pinned once, and the page's picks and notes change as the study registered.
